Question 1
?

A=[3−16−23−1−62],b=[−2014].

Consider the matrix A and vector b shown above. If the general least-squares solution of Ax=b is [a0]+x2[bc],x2∈R, what is the value of −10a+6bc?

a
5
b
13
c
7
d
310
e
6
Submit

decision.explanation: The second column is −1/3 times the first. Writing u=(3,6,3,−6)^T, least squares requires x₁−x₂/3=(uᵀb)/(uᵀu)=−27/90=−3/10. Thus a=−3/10 and the nullspace direction satisfies b/c=1/3. Therefore −10a+6b/c=3+2=5.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 6 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 \\ -6 & 2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $-10a+\frac{6b}{c}?$
after.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 3 & -6 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 6 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 \\ -6 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 3 & -6 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}90 & -30 \\ -30 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-27 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}90 & -30 & -27 \\ -30 & 10 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}90 & -30 & -27 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have  

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{3}{10}+\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{10}+\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{10} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
-10a+\frac{6b}{c}=-10\cdot (-\frac{3}{10})+\frac{6\cdot (\frac{1}{3})}{1}=5.
$$

decision.explanation: Let u=(2,1,−5)ᵀ. Since the second column is −2u, least squares requires x₁−2x₂=(uᵀb)/(uᵀu)=−15/30=−1/2. Therefore x₁=−1/2+2x₂, so a=−1/2 and b/c=2. Thus −2a+b/c=1+2=3.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 \\ -5 & 10\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $-2a+\frac{b}{c}?$
after.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -5 \\ -4 & -2 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 \\ -5 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -5 \\ -4 & -2 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}30 & -60 \\ -60 & 120\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ 30\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ -2 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}+2{x}_{2}.
$$

 Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}+2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
-2a+\frac{b}{c}=-2\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})+\frac{2}{1}=3.
$$

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 \\ -5 & 10\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $-2a+\frac{b}{c}?$
content.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -5 \\ -4 & -2 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 \\ -5 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -5 \\ -4 & -2 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}30 & -60 \\ -60 & 120\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ 30\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ -2 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}+2{x}_{2}.
$$

 Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}+2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
-2a+\frac{b}{c}=-2\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})+\frac{2}{1}=3.
$$
